t:
(a) In General.—Chapter 33 of title 18, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:


“§ 716. Police badges

“(a) Whoever—
“(1) knowingly transfers, transports, or receives, in interstate or foreign commerce, a counterfeit police badge;
“(2) knowingly transfers, in interstate or foreign commerce, a genuine police badge to an individual, knowing that such individual is not authorized to possess it under the law of the place in which the badge is the official badge of the police;
“(3) knowingly receives a genuine police badge in a transfer prohibited by paragraph (2); or
“(4) being a person not authorized to possess a genuine police badge under the law of the place in which the badge is the official badge of the police, knowingly transports that badge in interstate or foreign commerce,
shall be fined under this title or imprisoned not more than 6 months, or both.


“(b) It is a defense to a prosecution under this section that the badge is used or is intended to be used exclusively—
“(1) as a memento, or in a collection or exhibit;
“(2) for decorative purposes;
“(3) for a dramatic presentation, such as a theatrical, film, or television production; or
“(4) for any other recreational purpose.


“(c) As used in this section—
“(1) the term ‘genuine police badge’ means an official badge issued by public authority to identify an individual as a law enforcement officer having police powers; and
“(2) the term ‘counterfeit police badge’ means an item that so resembles a police badge that it would deceive an ordinary individual into believing it was a genuine police badge.”.



 
    (b) Clerical Amendment.—The table of sections at the beginning of chapter 33 of title 18, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new item:


“716. Police badges.”.

fable.w: This section creates a federal criminal offense for trafficking in counterfeit or unauthorized police badges, with defenses and definitions. The tempting reading is that the reference to "the law of the place" or the "defense to a prosecution" brings in outside parties, but these only define elements of the crime and a criminal defense. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue over or object to a federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section establishes criminal penalties for the illegal transfer, transport, or receipt of police badges. It defines offenses and defenses but does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties in a federal decision-making process. There are no advisory boards, public comment periods, or consultations with states or tribes mentioned.
qwen_block.s: Whoever— (1) knowingly transfers, transports, or receives, in interstate or foreign commerce, a counterfeit police badge; (2) knowingly transfers, in interstate or foreign commerce, a genuine police badge to an individual, knowing that such individual is not authorized to possess it under the law of the place in which the badge is the official badge of the police; (3) knowingly receives a genuine police badge in a transfer prohibited by paragraph (2); or (4) being a person not authorized to possess a genuine police badge under the law of the place in which the badge is the official badge of the police, knowingly transports that badge in interstate or foreign commerce, shall be fined under this title or imprisoned not more than 6 months, or both.

opus.w: This section creates a federal crime for trafficking in counterfeit or unauthorized police badges, and it amends a table of sections. It includes no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outsiders, or rulemaking authority. One could misread the affirmative 'defense to a prosecution' as a way for outsiders to challenge the government, or the reference to state 'law of the place' as coordination with states. Neither fits: a criminal defendant's defense is not a right to sue over a federal policy decision, and referring to state law does not involve states in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section creates a criminal offense regarding the transfer or transport of counterfeit or unauthorized genuine police badges. It defines terms and establishes penalties but does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) in a federal decision-making process. The mention of 'public authority' is strictly within the definition of a badge, not a procedural requirement for government action.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the definition of "genuine police badge" involves "public authority," implying some government interaction. However, this is merely a definitional clause for a criminal statute and does not establish a process for outside parties to participate in federal decision-making.
